_comment: Claude Code hook registrations this repo OWNS. install.sh merges these into
~/.claude/settings.json (add-only: never removes, never edits an existing entry).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Stow deploys the hook SCRIPTS into ~/.claude/hooks/, but a
script there is inert until settings.json REGISTERS it. Before 2026-09-05 nothing
did that -- install.sh had zero mentions of .claude -- so every new hook had to be
hand-wired into a 44KB machine-local JSON file on each machine, and in practice was
not. Surfaced when the Intel MacBook showed enforce-herdr-skill.sh unlinked.
WHY IT IS NOT UNDER home/. settings.json is machine-local (model, MCP servers, voice,
PAI config) and can never be stowed wholesale. settings/ is this repo's established
home for installer-driven, NOT-stow-managed config -- same as settings/iterm2 and
settings/wezterm. Keeping it out of home/ also stops stow from linking a manifest
into ~/.claude/hooks/ where Claude Code would see a stray file.
SCHEMA of each entry in "hooks":
event    required. A Claude Code hook event (PreToolUse, PostToolUse,
SessionStart, ...).
matcher  OPTIONAL. Tool name to match, e.g. Bash, Grep, Skill. OMIT IT for
events that have no tool to match on -- SessionStart's real groups
in settings.json carry no matcher key, and inventing one would be a
shape Claude Code has never been handed. Omitting it also widens the
already-registered test from (event, matcher, command) to (event,
command) across ALL groups, which is the correct question for this
class: two copies of a session-start hook is never right, it is the
watcher running twice.
script   required. Display name, and the basename looked for under
~/.claude/hooks/ unless script_path overrides that. Gate: if the
file is not on disk the entry is SKIPPED -- registering a hook whose
script is missing turns every matching tool call into an error.
script_path  OPTIONAL. Where the file ACTUALLY lives, when it is not in
~/.claude/hooks/. May use $HOME. The session-start watchers are
ordinary CLI tools stowed to ~/.local/bin -- they are run BY a hook
entry, they are not hook scripts. Without this they were skipped
forever, on every machine, with a 'not deployed' reason that was
simply untrue.
entry    required. Written into settings.json verbatim. Must use $HOME, never a
literal username, so the same JSON works on every machine.
requires optional. Paths that must exist before the entry is registered. THIS IS
A SAFETY GATE, not decoration -- see enforce-herdr-skill below.
targets  OPTIONAL. Which settings files this entry is registered into.
OMITTING IT MEANS ["user"] -- ~/.claude/settings.json only, which is
what every entry did before 2026-09-19 and what almost every entry
should keep doing. The vocabulary is EXACTLY the --target flag's:
user     ~/.claude/settings.json
project  ~/.claude/settings.project.json
WHY IT EXISTS. The pj launcher passes --setting-sources project,local,
so the USER source never loads and none of its SessionStart hooks
register. ci-watch is the escalating CI-red alarm and pj is the daily
launcher, so under pj the alarm was silent -- and a silent alarm is
indistinguishable from a healthy one, which is the exact failure the
_sessionstart_note below was written about.
DECLARE IT HERE, NEVER TWICE. The alternative considered on
2026-09-19 was a second copy of the command inside a templated
settings.project.json. is_registered() compares the command string
EXACTLY, so two copies that drift by one character stop matching and
the next sync appends a duplicate instead of noticing.
NOT FOR LifeOS HOOKS. This manifest is dotfiles-owned. A hook that
belongs to LifeOS stays registered by LifeOS; routing one through
here would move its ownership across the boundary.
why      required. One line, printed when the entry is skipped.
MATCH RULE (install.sh): an entry counts as already registered when the triple
(event, matcher, entry.command) matches something already present. Never the
command alone -- the same script legitimately appears under several matchers.

hooks.why: DENIES a Bash command that would print a credential-named variable into the transcript (the ${V:-word} probe, env dumps, bare echo). Was hand-wired into settings.json until 2026-09-20; this entry matches that command byte-for-byte
Shouts when a grep/rg is used to CONCLUDE instead of census.py
Same guard on the Grep tool, not just shell greps
Blocks herdr commands until the herdr skill is read this session
Lifts the block above; pointless without the skill it watches for
Escalating CI-red alarm on the session dashboard
The 20-line start card for pj sessions (D-20260920-04): open items, wrap-up warning, handoff pointer, hello rule. Project target only: pj is the launcher it serves

F3 (W-20260921-13): reads the running claude's argv via CLAUDE_PID and prints ONE LAUNCH WARNING line when the appended prompt file is not the pj-prompt-file cache (RULES.md missing), a plugin dir is absent or --setting-sources drifted; silent on a match; always appends one line to ~/.local/state/pj/launches.log. Separate from the read-only card on purpose (P5.2). Project target only
Writes the no-wrap-up flag the start card reads when a pj session that did real work ends without /pj:wrap-up (D-20260920-03). Project target only, same as the card

Escalating capture-PRESENCE alarm (narrowed 2026-09-07: no ccw doctor call). Is ccw installed, at/above floor, plugin enabled, plugin copy on disk. Capture died silently for ten days once. Project target added 2026-09-21 (P5.6): cc-capture runs under pj, so its alarm must too

DENIES rm -rf / or ~, force push to main/master, bare git reset --hard, git clean -fd. Moved from the dotfiles project settings 2026-09-21 (P5.6): the rule is OPERATIONAL_RULES Deletion, machine-wide. Project target only: c sessions keep LifeOS's own set

DENIES bare pip/python/pytest/ruff in favour of uv. Moved 2026-09-21 (P5.6): the rule is OPERATIONAL_RULES Environment and every project CLAUDE.md. 0 of 51 and 1 of 245 recent commands elsewhere would have been denied, the 1 correctly

DENIES npm/yarn/npx in favour of pnpm or bun. Moved 2026-09-21 (P5.6): the package-manager policy is machine-wide (.zshrc wrappers block the same in every shell). 0 would-denies in 296 recent commands elsewhere

DENIES gh auth login / setup-git / refresh, which re-add HTTPS credential helpers and break SSH-only auth (D-20260917-09). F1 travelled the census, secret-probe and herdr guards and MISSED this one: it was registered only in ~/.claude/settings.json (user, so c only) and in this repo's own .claude/settings.json (so pj only HERE). Under pj in any other project nothing registered it -- measured at P6b. script_path points at the EXISTING dot-claude file rather than stowing a copy: the two copies are byte-identical (verified 2026-09-21, sha 58a9712ed1c1, 4715 b), that path is already occupied so stow would conflict, and nothing in dot-claude is edited. Project target only, and this repo's own entry is removed in the same commit, so it fires ONCE per session, not twice

WARNS when the session's cwd is a subdirectory of a hub root, so opening a subdir does not spawn a fresh empty memory store and re-scatter memory. Carried under pj at the P8b gate 2026-09-21: its HUB_ROOTS list holds exactly one path, and that path is a pj project, so the guard was aimed squarely at pj sessions and fired in none of them. LifeOS's file, reached by script_path, not copied. Never blocks: always exits 0

STATES the voice contract before the reply is written and names what the previous reply broke. pj-voice V4 says zero em dashes; measured across 17 pj transcripts, 371 of them in 174,107 characters of prose, while every other voice rule was obeyed. The wording is not the fault: DA_IDENTITY.md says almost the same words and the `c` control set has ZERO, because the `c` family also runs DriftReminder.hook.ts, which counts. That hook is registered only in ~/.claude/settings.json and pj passes --setting-sources project,local, so it has never fired here -- its contract line appears twice in a `c` transcript and zero times in 35.3 MB of pj transcript. UserPromptSubmit and not Stop, on DriftReminder's own recorded measurement: a Stop hook fires after the text is on screen, and FormatGate going observation-only took drift from 0% across 168 turns to 61-91% across 2,608. DriftReminder itself is NOT carried: its contract is hardcoded to a banner, a closer and max 2 em dashes, none of which pj has, and its only seam is LIFEOS_DIR. First UserPromptSubmit entry in this manifest. Project target only. Never blocks: every path exits 0. Ruled by Gavin at the P9 gate 2026-09-22

Records the session's herdr agent state. Carried under pj at the P8b gate 2026-09-21: pj sessions run inside herdr panes, and this fired only under c. HERDR OWNS THIS FILE and rewrites it on integration update (its header says so), which is exactly why the entry points at its path via script_path instead of stowing a copy that would go stale silently. The `session` argument matches the user-level registration's shape

_traveller_note: THE test -x ... || true SHAPE ON A PreToolUse GUARD IS DELIBERATE. A deny is JSON on
stdout under exit 0, so the guard still denies through it; and a registration that
outlives its script (this tool is add-only) costs nothing instead of turning every
Bash call into a hook error. That is also what makes a rollback safe: restore the
manifest and the scripts, and any entry left behind in the rendered file self-gates.
PROJECT-ONLY TRAVELLERS LEAVE THIS REPO'S .claude/settings.json. One firing per
session, not two. A c session in this repo therefore no longer has them; LifeOS can
register the stowed path itself if it wants them under c (note in the P5.6 report).
_sessionstart_note: THE COMMAND STRINGS ABOVE ARE COPIED BYTE-FOR-BYTE FROM THE LIVE settings.json.
That is not fussiness. is_registered() compares the command EXACTLY, so a
cosmetic difference -- dropping the test -x guard, unquoting the path, changing
the timeout -- reads as 'not registered' and appends a SECOND copy. On this Mac
that would mean ci-watch and ccw-watch running twice at every session start.
If you ever reword one of these, reword it in settings.json first and copy it
back, never the other way round.
NO requires GATE, DELIBERATELY. These commands self-gate: `test -x <path> && ...
|| true` is a no-op returning success when the tool is absent. Gate 1 already
refuses to register them when the file is missing; the command shape means even
a stale registration on a machine that later loses the tool costs nothing.
WHY THESE TWO WERE MISSING UNTIL 2026-09-06. They were hand-wired into this
Mac's settings.json on 2026-08-18 (commit 1ec3d66 says so in its own message:
'outside this repo'), and the manifest shipped on 2026-09-05 had no SessionStart
entry of any kind. So the whole ALARM class was stowed-but-unregistered while
the GUARD class was automated -- the wrong half. A missing guard fails toward
'something was not blocked', which shows up in behaviour. A missing alarm fails
toward silence, and silence is indistinguishable from health. That is the exact
failure ccw-watch exists to catch, and it was happening to ccw-watch.
_requires_note: The requires gate on enforce-herdr-skill.sh is load-bearing, and it is the reason
this manifest has a requires field at all.
That hook DENIES every `herdr` Bash command until the herdr skill is invoked in the
session. The only thing that lifts the block is the sibling PostToolUse hook seeing
the herdr skill actually run. ~/.claude/skills/herdr is a symlink into ~/.agents/,
is NOT tracked by this repo, and nothing deploys it.
So on a machine with the hook registered and no skill installed, herdr is blocked
PERMANENTLY inside Claude, with no way to unlock it. The laptop is exactly the box
that drives herdr against the mini, which is how this was caught before shipping
